title: The Iran War Widens: Yemen, Hormuz and What Comes Next
gist: Al-Monitor video panel (Sept. 17, 2026) on the widening US-Iran war covering the state of US-Iran talks, Iran's internal nuclear debate, the effect of US midterms, and regime staying power; the page contains only the agenda, not the discussion content.

insights.claim: Al-Monitor frames the key near-term flashpoints of the US-Iran war as Yemen and the Strait of Hormuz, with diplomacy and de-escalation prospects tied to the UN leaders' gathering and the run-up to November.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Late September UNGA and the November US midterms are the calendar catalysts to watch for shifts in the war.

insights.claim: Iran's internal debate over its nuclear program is described as having evolved during the war, flagged as a key question for analysts.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: A shift in Iran's nuclear stance would change escalation odds; monitor for signals of weaponization debate.

insights.claim: The US midterms are identified as a potential variable for Iran policy, raising the question of what could change and what would stay the same.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: US election outcomes could alter war policy; position for volatility around November.

insights.claim: The panel treats the war as a test of the Iranian regime's staying power and its succession/leadership outlook.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Regime-stability questions are the tail risk behind any Iran-exposed position.
